title: Machine-learning alerts increase referrals for epilepsy surgery evaluation in a randomized trial
summary: At one specialized pediatric epilepsy center, an NLP support system using an SVM and n-gram features screened neurology notes and randomized providers of 284 identified potential candidates to receive an alert or usual care. During a median 24-month follow-up, presurgical evaluation referrals were 9.8% with alerts and 3.1% in controls (adjusted HR 3.21; 95% CI 0.95–10.8; one-sided p=.03); nine alert-group children and no controls underwent surgery. The trial was prospective and randomized, but involved one center, had a wide confidence interval, and used one-sided testing; it does not establish benefit across other settings.
ai_technology: Natural-language processing with a supervised support vector machine and n-gram features

evidence.tested: A prospective randomized trial compared provider alerts with standard care among 300 potential candidates at 14 outpatient clinic sites of one pediatric epilepsy center; presurgical referrals and subsequent surgery were recorded.
evidence.unknown: Generalizability beyond the specialized center and the effect in other care settings were not established. The referral estimate was imprecise, and the paper reports one-sided p values.
evidence.ai_role: An NLP/SVM system screened free-text EHR neurology notes for potential surgical candidates and generated provider alerts.

source_review.scope: Full primary publisher article, including Methods, Results, author affiliations and publication history
